messages:
Maria S: heads-up — customer reported they suddenly lost access to compliance logs in Console. They hit 403 on the /v1/compliance/logs endpoint. Ticket #CS-19872.

Maria S: original error from their curl:
```
curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \n  \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/compliance/logs?since=2026-03-10\"
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json

{
  \"error\": \"forbidden\",
  \"message\": \"missing_scope\",
  \"required_scope\": \"compliance.logs:read\"
}
```

Maria S: they say nothing changed on their side other than an Okta group rename last week. Can identity folks advise?

Jason E: on it. first guess is SSO claim mapping lost the scope. Ask them to paste decoded token payload (just the scp claim).

Laura Support: asked customer for token dump (redacted). They provided payload: 
```json
{
  "sub": "00u123exampleuser",
  "iss": "https://acme.okta.com/oauth2/default",
  "scp": ["openid","profile"],
  "exp": 1768507000
}
```

Laura Support: notice there is no "compliance.logs:read" scope in scp. They used to have it via group-to-scope mapping.

Evan Sec: this matches a policy change we rolled that tightened which groups map to the compliance scopes. I need the org id and a sample org role mapping. Maria — can you confirm org_id for the customer?

Maria S: org_id = org_0aCMe. I also asked them to check their entitlement page under Console > Org > Entitlements — they reported seeing no "Compliance log read" entitlement listed for any of their roles.

Sam Identity Bot: identity-service alert: mapping change deployed 2026-02-28 18:07 UTC. Affected mapping: okta-group-compliance-read -> compliance_reader role (was set to disabled).

Evan Sec: ok, looks like the mapping was accidentally toggled off during the Okta group rename rollout. Fix plan: re-enable mapping and force re-issue of SSO tokens (or ask customer to sign out and back in). I can push a mapping change but need approval for immediate hotfix.

Jason E: if we re-enable mapping, existing tokens won't magically gain scopes. We'll need to force a token refresh. We can also create a short-lived service-token for them to repro immediately. Suggest steps I used to validate locally: 
```bash
# introspect token to confirm scopes
curl -X POST -u \"$CLIENT_ID:$CLIENT_SECRET\" \
  -d \"token=$TOKEN\" https://auth.redwood.ai/oauth2/introspect | jq .

# attempt read and show 403 body
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \
  \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/compliance/logs?limit=1\" -v
```

Jason E: sample introspect output we expect when broken: 
```json
{
  "active": true,
  "scope": "openid profile",
  "client_id": "acme-ui",
  "exp": 1768507000
}
```

Jason E: when mapping is correct it should contain: 
```json
{
  "active": true,
  "scope": "openid profile compliance.logs:read",
  "client_id": "acme-ui",
  "exp": 1768507300
}
```

Laura Support: customer tried sign-out/sign-in and still no scopes. They didn't get a new token after sign-in (prob due to cached session at Okta). They will do a hard logout.

Evan Sec: I'm pushing mapping re-enable now. Deploy Bot: starting identity mapping update job.

Deploy Bot: identity-mapping-service v1.24.3 deployed (canary -> stable) — change id map-2026-02-28-regen applied.

Evan Sec: mapping re-enabled. Maria, can you ask customer to do a full browser clear + re-auth, then paste introspect output? If they can't, we can issue a temporary service token scoped to compliance.logs:read for troubleshooting.

Maria S: asked customer to clear, re-auth, and provide introspect. They responded with new introspect output (redacted):
```json
{
  "active": true,
  "scope": "openid profile compliance.logs:read",
  "client_id": "acme-ui"
}
```

Laura Support: after they tried again with new token, curl returned 200 and logs payload. Customer confirms they can view Console audit history now.

Maria S: quick root cause summary for ticket: Okta group rename caused identity mapping to be disabled during a mapping cleanup deploy, which removed the compliance scope from tokens. Re-enable mapping and force re-auth fixes the issue. Recommend we: 1) add an automated smoke test that hits /v1/compliance/logs with a test org to verify scope mapping after mapping deploys, 2) document the group-naming migration steps to avoid toggling mapping off.

Evan Sec: agree on smoke test. I'll open a follow-up infra ticket to add mapping validation to our deploy CI.

Jason E: for immediate mitigation we should add a monitoring alert for 403 rates on /v1/compliance/logs per org > threshold. I'll draft an alert.

Maria S: closing CS-19872 as resolved with steps noted. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Laura Support: marking ticket resolved in Zendesk and adding runbook snippet to internal KB: "If compliance logs 403 -> introspect token -> check scp claim -> check entitlement mapping -> re-enable mapping -> force re-auth."

Evan Sec: added follow-up infra ticket INFRA-3145.

Maria S: closing thread.
